title: Signal and Rumour
briefing: Conflicting claims about water, hospital access and supply allocation are overwhelming official channels. Some warnings are fabricated; others describe real delays. Residents need usable instructions now, but verification teams cannot investigate every report before the next shift change.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: A reserved alert channel can reach most phones within four minutes. Community relays are slower but do not depend on the overloaded central dispatch system; publishing raw logs diverts repair staff into redaction work.
private_intelligence.community: Two earlier alerts used language residents understood as a guarantee, then changed. Trusted local groups can reach people who mute official notifications, but those groups disagree about acceptable instructions.
private_intelligence.economy: A broad broadcast is inexpensive compared with verifying and releasing service records. Uncertainty already delays orders; local relay funding has a smaller cost but leaves firms waiting for a unified position.
private_intelligence.safety: A forged evacuation image is circulating near a real damaged access road. Fast instructions can prevent injuries, but a blanket message may direct residents away from safer local alternatives.

choices.title: Reserve a Single Alert Channel
choices.description: Issue one mandatory citywide instruction set and reserve dispatch bandwidth for it while verification continues.
choices.consequence: Rapid instructions reduce immediate harm and steady dispatch operations. Commercial interruptions cost money, and another centrally imposed message without full evidence sharply erodes confidence.

choices.title: Publish Verified Service Logs
choices.description: Release a checked incident timeline, clearly label uncertainty, and delay new directives until verification is complete.
choices.consequence: Visible evidence restores legitimacy. Verification consumes repair capacity and funding, while the delay leaves residents exposed to unresolved hazards.

choices.title: Fund Trusted Local Relays
choices.description: Give neighbourhood groups bounded safety guidance, local updates and resources to reach residents directly.
choices.consequence: Local messengers rebuild confidence and help people avoid harm. Supporting the relays costs money and pulls technical staff from recovery, while uneven reach limits the safety gain.
